key_insight: Cardiologent turns arrhythmia assessment into a patient-level decision workflow, combining signal reading, patient context, and guideline-based reasoning to decide not just what rhythm is present, but what it means and what to do next.
clinical_relevance: This matters because the same arrhythmia can imply very different urgency and management depending on the patient, making context-aware, auditable decision support more clinically useful than label-only detection.
method: Uses multiple agents to analyze a single ECG lead and a wearable photoplethysmogram window with measured features.
Assembles window-level readings into a patient rhythm profile, then reasons over patient data plus retrieved clinical guidelines.
Adds a critic agent to check each conclusion against the cited guideline before producing the final decision.
evidence_signal: The system was evaluated on integrated diagnosis, clinical significance, and urgency/management, and it scored highest across all patient-level tasks under both cardiologists and an LLM judge, with judge agreement similar to cardiologist inter-rater agreement (ICC 0.74/0.66 vs 0.67).
watch_item: Because the system depends on retrieved guidelines and expert-validated reasoning, real-world performance may still vary with guideline coverage, data quality, and workflow integration.
paper_title: Cardiologent: Multi-Agent Clinical Decision Support for Patient-Level Arrhythmia Assessment, Urgency, and Management
